lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Measurement: Time, Liquid Volume, and Mass
lessonRef.focus: measurement problems solved by multiplication and division
lessonRef.title: Applied problem solving: measurement problems solved by multiplication and division

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the problem below asks for.

items.prompt: A jug has 350 milliliters. Another 120 milliliters are poured in. How much is in the jug now?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what the problem is asking before you compute.

items.prompt: A gardener has 56 seeds and plants the same number in each of 8 pots. How many seeds go in each pot?
A container has 180 kilograms. 121 kilograms are removed. How many kilograms are left?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A garden has 5 rows with 3 plants in each row. How many plants are there?
A container has 215 grams. 159 grams are removed. How many grams are left?
A gardener has 21 seeds and plants the same number in each of 3 pots. How many seeds go in each pot?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A container has 558 grams. Another 255 grams are poured in. How many grams are in the container now?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A garden has 3 rows with 2 plants in each row. How many plants are there?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
